property_summary: After the fallback call, pastBlockTime must be strictly greater than the timestamp when the call was made.
After a successful fallback call that does not trigger the self-destruct, pastBlockTime is never greater than block.timestamp + 1.
After the last fallback call, pastBlockTime is always exactly block.timestamp + 1 when the call does not trigger the if(block.number % 15 == 0) branch.
After any sequence of public calls ending with a payable fallback, if the fallback did not revert then pastBlockTime increases by at least 1.
After any call to the fallback function that succeeds, the contract's balance must be a multiple of 10 ether if the block number is not a multiple of 15, otherwise it must be 0.
The fallback function must not succeed when called at the same block timestamp as the previous successful call.
Every successful fallback call strictly increases the recorded pastBlockTime.
The fallback function must not allow two successful calls at the same block timestamp.
The fallback function must revert when called at the same block timestamp as the previous successful call.
A successful fallback call must not be followed by another successful fallback call at the same block number.
After a successful fallback call, the contract's balance should be zero when the block number is divisible by 15.
After a successful fallback call, the contract's balance should be zero when the block number is NOT divisible by 15.
If the fallback succeeds, the contract's balance is zero when returning from the fallback call and the last transfer condition (block.number % 15 != 0) is true, else it retains the surplus.

After any successful fallback call (reverts on msg.value != 10 or timestamp <= pastBlockTime), the contract's balance is unchanged if the block number satisfies the transfer condition, else it is zero.
After any successful fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether, the contract's balance modulo 10 ether equals 10 ether if the block number is not divisible by 15, else it equals 0.

After any call to fallback with msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the contract's balance should always equal (msg.sender.balance + 10 ether - pastBlockTime delta) if block.number % 15 == 0, otherwise it remains the same.

After a successful fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the contract's balance should decrease by exactly address(this).balance if block.number % 15 == 0, otherwise it should remain unchanged.

After a fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, if block.number % 15 == 0 then the contract's balance must be zero (all balance transferred out), otherwise it increases by 10 ether.

When fallback is called with msg.value = 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, and block.number % 15 == 0, the contract's balance after the call must be less than the caller's initial balance plus 10 ether (for reference version it becomes zero, for buggy version it still has 1 ether).
After a successful call to fallback with exactly 10 ether, the contract's address balance changes only if block.number % 15 == 0; otherwise it stays the same.
